subject.title: [Feature]: Add one-way dispatch mode for A2A handoffs without reply-back ping-pong

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit one-way A2A dispatch semantic to `sessions_send`, and should that be a per-call mode on the existing tool or a separate primitive?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but the permanent tool/API shape affects core session semantics, docs, tests, and compatibility with existing A2A conversation workflows.

options.title: Add per-call dispatch mode
options.body: Add a narrow explicit `sessions_send` delivery mode that skips requester ping-pong and target announce unless requested while keeping the current default unchanged.

options.title: Add a separate primitive
options.body: Introduce a new one-way delivery tool or primitive and keep `sessions_send` as the conversation-oriented API, accepting a larger new surface.

options.title: Defer to narrower fixes
options.body: Keep this open as design context while landing reverse-call, cycle, acknowledgement, and channel-specific fixes without adding dispatch semantics yet.

recommendation.title: Add per-call dispatch mode
recommendation.body: Add a narrow explicit `sessions_send` delivery mode that skips requester ping-pong and target announce unless requested while keeping the current default unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest inspected history signal for multi-agent routing and the core sessions product boundary, so he is the best available owner for the API-direction choice.
